Resolves #20472

Fetch now sends supplied headers instead of only echoing them in `response.request`. Existing connection defaults are merged with per-request values using case-insensitive native Headers semantics, without mutating either input. Invalid header inputs reject the returned promise. `Neo.Fetch` inherits the repair.

Evidence: native HTTP plus real Chromium App/Data-worker Pipelines; all close-target behavior is exercised. No deployment or credential change.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `FetchRequestHeaders.spec.mjs` observes both URL forms, default/request precedence, tuples and native Headers at HTTP. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: no-header POST and non-OK controls, plus existing `FetchRequestMetadata.spec.mjs` and `UrlResolution.spec.mjs`. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `PipelineFetchHeaders.spec.mjs` records actual HTTP headers from App and Data workers and checks the next no-header read. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. The method remains promise-based so native header validation rejects asynchronously. Across workers, callers use serializable records or tuple lists. Defaults apply to every URL requested by the instance, including all shared Neo.Fetch singleton requests; the JSDoc now states that scope. Pipeline interceptor behavior remains in #9553.

## Test Evidence

The [retained red control](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20472#issuecomment-6691057619) failed six header cases on the old source while the ordinary POST/body control passed. After the repair, focused connection tests and the [real-worker HTTP witness](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20472#issuecomment-6691163545) pass. All added coverage runs in CI.

Change class: restoration. `agent-preflight` is not hosted here; the local hooks and PR Baseline provide the applicable checks.

## Post-Merge Validation

No separate acceptance remains. #9553 stays open for the full interceptor feature.

- `637a4e3a70` — repair native header dispatch and pin HTTP/worker behavior.
- `aca778af18` — clarify the default-header scope after review.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #20472 (Contract Ledger, AC-1..3); `src/data/connection/Fetch.mjs` at `dev`, where `request` hands native `fetch` only `{body, method}` (lines 118–121) while `response.request` echoes the config; the Xhr precedent (`Xhr.mjs:179`, an object-spread merge that is not case-insensitive); the `Neo.Fetch` facade (`src/Fetch.mjs`, `remote.app` methods). I wrote the premise down before opening the diff.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:**
    - One native `Headers` built from `defaultHeaders`, then `set` for each per-request entry, so the override is case-insensitive by Headers semantics.
    - A guard for the `null` default, because `new Headers(null)` throws. No mutation of either input, and nothing hardcoded (no Authorization special case, no name lists).
    - Tests that observe headers at a real endpoint (ephemeral port, connections destroyed), with real App and Data worker Pipelines for AC-3.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches.
    - `new Headers(this.defaultHeaders ?? undefined)` covers the guard.
    - `new Headers(config.headers ?? undefined).forEach((value, name) => headers.set(name, value))` gives the case-insensitive override, accepts all three init forms, and copies instead of mutating.
    - `headers` is passed in both URL forms.
    - The one thing beyond my premise: `request` became `async`, so an invalid header name rejects the returned promise instead of throwing synchronously. It is pinned by its own test.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The defect was proven at the wire, not inferred from echoed metadata, and the tests keep it that way.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (non-blocking): `defaultHeaders` has been dead until now, and on the shared `Neo.Fetch` singleton it now applies to every URL that singleton requests. That includes `manager/rpc/Message.mjs:209`'s RPC posts and any cross-origin endpoint. A consumer setting `Neo.Fetch.defaultHeaders = {Authorization: …}` would send the credential to every origin, and any custom default triggers CORS preflights wherever it applies. A per-connection instance (a Pipeline's `connection`) scopes it to one URL, which is the safe use. This matches Xhr's existing semantics, so it is not a defect. One sentence in the `defaultHeaders` JSDoc naming that scope would close it.
- **Documented search:**
  - In-tree callers that already pass headers to a Fetch connection, whose requests would now change: none. The RPC manager passes `{}`, and the realworld apps use `Neo.Xhr`.
  - Header leakage between reads: the component control read observes `null` at the endpoint.
  - The `null` default throwing: guarded.
  - Duplicate-name joins from an object spread: avoided by `set`.
